paragraphs: Here's the big idea, friend. Laodicea looked at itself and said, "I am rich; I have grown wealthy and need nothing" (Rev 3:17). Jesus looked at the same church and saw something else. They were "wretched, pitiful, poor, blind, and naked" (Rev 3:17). The most dangerous place to be is thinking you've got it all together when you don't.

Now here's the part that gets me. Jesus doesn't walk away. He says, "Those I love I rebuke and discipline. Therefore be earnest and repent" (Rev 3:19). The hard words come from love, and the fix is real: gold, white garments and salve, all offered by Him (Rev 3:18). So when His Word stings a little, baker, don't run from the sting. That's Him loving you enough to tell you the truth.

And then LISTEN to this. "Behold, I stand at the door and knock. If anyone hears My voice and opens the door, I will come in and dine with him, and he with Me" (Rev 3:20). Jesus isn't just correcting, He's inviting you to the table. He also promises the one who overcomes a seat with Him on His throne (Rev 3:21), and that's why my ovens stay ready. That's the last letter of the seven, and the Spirit's word to every church is to listen (Rev 3:22).
